stem:
Which part of the sentence has an error? If the sentence is correct, choose "No error".

One of the printers in the records section are out of ink again.
hints: The subject is not always the noun closest to the verb. Ask: how many things are out of ink?
Cover the words "of the printers in the records section". What word is left as the subject?
In "one of the …", the subject is "one", which is singular. Match the verb to "one", then check the other parts.

solution.methodName: Find the true subject, then match the verb

steps.why: "Of the printers" and "in the records section" are extra phrases that describe "one". The verb never agrees with a noun inside an "of" phrase.

steps.action: "One" is singular, so the verb must be singular: "is".
steps.why: Read it without the extra words: "One … is out of ink."

steps.action: Check "One of the printers". It is correct: after "one of the", the noun is plural, because you pick one from a group.
Check "in the records section". It only tells where the printer is, and it is correct.
The error is "are out of ink". It should be "is out of ink".

trapNotes.One of the printers: Some learners think "printers" should be "printer". But after "one of the", the noun is always plural: one of the printers, one of the clerks.
trapNotes.in the records section: This phrase only tells where the printer is. It has no error. Its job is to sit between the subject and the verb and distract you.
trapNotes.No error: "Are" sounds right because "printers" is plural and sits near the verb. But the subject is "one", so the verb must be "is".
